extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and policymakers interested in postwar planning
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and report the recommendations and policy standards for postwar demobilization, contract terminations, surplus property disposal, and related administrative reforms as presented in a published index of recommendations. The page is a newspaper report summarizing a detailed set of numbered policy prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified government handling of human demobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: That the government forces dealing with the human problems of demobilization be unified on two fronts—the executive and Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to coordinate responsibilities between the executive branch and Congress to handle human problems of transition from war to peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of a 'work director' in Office of War Mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation in the Office of War Mobilization of the new post of 'work director' to 'see that the human side of demobilization is not forgotten.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An executive-level post focused specifically on human adjustment issues in demobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for the 'work director'
rubrics_metrics.description: This 'work director' to be a man 'of such outstanding caliber as to command the immediate confidence of the country.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes selection of a highly respected, authoritative individual to lead human-side demobilization efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work director to collaborate with Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: This 'work director' to work with Congress in the development of a combined program of legislation and operations 'to carry out the objectives that all of us share.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for joint executive-legislative planning and coordination on demobilization legislation and operational programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of work director's responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields to be covered: personnel demobilization of the armed forces; developing adequate machinery for job placement of veterans and demobilized war workers; adequate care for returning veterans; physical and occupational therapy for wounded and disabled; resumption of educational training interrupted by war; vocational training; special employment problems of the great war industries, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad mandate addressing employment, medical/rehabilitation, education/training, and industry-specific employment transition issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single community point for returning servicemembers
rubrics_metrics.description: That there be in each community only one place to which returning servicemen and servicewomen need to go to learn all their rights and get them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify access to benefits and information by creating a single local office for returning service personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial 'kit' to assure quick cash pending contract settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a complete 'financial kit' including immediate payments, loans, interest payments, and expedited settlement tools to assure quick cash pending contract settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A package of financial measures to prevent contractor insolvency and cash-flow problems during termination and settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate full payment for completed articles
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Immediate payment—the full 100 per cent—for all completed articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay contractors in full for finished goods immediately upon termination to ensure liquidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate payment for uncompleted contract portions (factual items and estimated costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) On the uncompleted portion of the contract immediate payment—the full 100 per cent—of the government's estimate of 'factual' items, where proof ordinarily is simple, such as direct labor or materials, and 2] other items on which the government is able to satisfy itself up to 90 per cent of the contractor's total estimated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prompt partial/full payments based on verifiable costs and high-percentage estimates to expedite settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate payment for subcontractor settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Immediate payment—the full 100 per cent—of settlements with subcontractors as soon as approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subcontractors receive prompt full payment once their settlement is approved to avoid cascading defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government payment of interest on termination claims
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Payment by the government of interest on termination claims until settled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensate contractors for time value of money during the settlement delay period.

rubrics_metrics.name: New simplified T-loans by local banks with government guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) As insurance against delays in validating claims, a new, simplified system of T (termination) loans by local banks, with government guaranties, to be available to all war contractors, primes and subs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate short-term bank lending to contractors backed by government guarantees to bridge settlement delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government direct loans if banks fail within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) For those unable to obtain such loans from their local banks in thirty days, the government to make the loans directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A government as-lender-of-last-resort provision to ensure timely liquidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of V and VT loans until T-loans authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: (g) Until the new T loans are authorized by Congress, extension of V and VT loans to all eligible borrowers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bridge existing loan programs to cover contractors until the new scheme is legally in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited settlements for hardship cases
rubrics_metrics.description: (h) Finally, for hardship cases unable to use any of the tools outlined above, expedited settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an accelerated settlement pathway for cases of acute hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick, fair and final settlement through negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick, fair and final settlement through negotiation by contractors and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes negotiated settlements to reach prompt and equitable conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Comptroller General review to fraud with administrative detection aids
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Review powers of Comptroller General limited to fraud with every administrative aid for detecting fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict exhaustive financial re‑scrutiny by the Comptroller General to fraud-suspect cases while providing tools to detect fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sizable settlements made by teams of negotiators
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) That all sizable settlements be made by teams of negotiators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-member negotiation teams to handle large settlements for robustness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiation teams must file written reports and keep full records
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) These teams to file written reports and keep full records of the bases of settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document negotiation rationale and bases to ensure transparency and enable oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractors to keep records for three years
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Contractors to keep records for three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record-keeping requirement to support audits or reviews for a defined retention period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add Comptroller General and Attorney General to Joint Contract Termination Board
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) That the Comptroller General and the Attorney General be added to the Joint Contract Termination Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include oversight and legal authorities on the termination board to coordinate review and legal perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further administrative safeguards under study
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) Further administrative safeguards now under study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates ongoing work to identify additional procedural protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish joint contract termination board within Office of War Mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment on an operating basis of a joint contract termination board within the Office of War Mobilization, to unify procedures and policies of all agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize and harmonize contract termination policies and procedures across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman of contract board to be independent civilian
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The board chairman to be a civilian, independent of any of the procurement agencies, answerable to the Director of War Mobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure independent civilian leadership for impartiality and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman to require progress reports and report to Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) This chairman to require progress reports from all agencies and to report regularly to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular reporting to maintain oversight and transparency of settlement progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board to monitor loan uptake (V, VT and T loans)
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Also to maintain a running survey of the extent to which V and VT loans and the new T loans are taken out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track utilization of loan programs to assess effectiveness and need for adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board to monitor all aspects of contract settlement and recommend changes
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) To keep a constant eye on all aspects of contract settlement, recommending any changes that become necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous oversight function with authority to suggest policy/procedure modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add War Production Board to joint contract board
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) The War Production Board be added to the joint contract board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include WPB representation for production-policy perspective in termination decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spread acceptance of uniform termination clause for fixed-price contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Spread acceptance by war contractors of the uniform termination article for fixed-price contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage-standardized contract clauses to simplify and harmonize termination settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative authorization to protect subcontractors on insolvency/default
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The procurement agencies to be authorized by legislation to protect subcontractors in event of insolvency or default of their customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authority to shield subcontractors from upstream bankruptcies or defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create standard termination clause for subcontractors
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) A standard termination article for subcontractors to be completed soon to supplement the uniform termination article for prime contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend standardized termination protections down the contract chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate nuisance‑sized claims below a minimum promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) A minimum figure to be set by the Director of War Mobilization below which 'nuisance-sized' claims can be immediately validated with suitable safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set a de minimis threshold to expedite small claims, with safeguards to prevent abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment with 'company-sized' settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Vigorous experiment with the so-called 'company-sized' type of settlement, seeking a workable plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot broader, company-level settlement approaches to streamline aggregate claim resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training schools for negotiators and contractor representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools to be set up around the country for training government negotiators and contractor representatives in the same classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint training to create shared understanding of negotiation processes and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt clearance of government property from private plants (60 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt clearance of government property from private plants not later than sixty days after the filing of inventory lists, manufacturers having the right to remove and store the property earlier at their own risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-limited requirement to clear government-furnished property, with option for contractors to act earlier at their risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate administrative implementation of termination program
rubrics_metrics.description: This entire termination program to be put into effect by the agencies at once to the extent administratively possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement recommendations without waiting for full legislative action where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt enactment of legislation to make termination program fully effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt enactment of legislation to make this program fully effective, including appropriate authority to permit company-wide settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek legislative backing for broader settlement powers (e.g., company-wide settlements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of surplus property administrator with full authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of War Mobilization to name a surplus property administrator in the Office of War Mobilization with full authority for handling every aspect of surplus disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize surplus-disposal authority in a single empowered administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish surplus property policy board with multi-agency representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A surplus property policy board with the administrator as chairman with full and final authority, and with War, Navy, Treasury, RFC, Maritime Commission, War Production Board, Bureau of the Budget, Food Administrator, Attorney General, Federal Works Agency, State Department and Foreign Economic Administration represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an interagency policy board to set disposal policies reflecting multiple government interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four major specialized outlets for disposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Four major outlets to handle actual disposal, each in a clearly defined field, with no overlappings: (a) consumer goods to Treasury Procurement Division; (b) capital and producer goods to a single corporation within the RFC; (c) ships and maritime property to Maritime Commission; (d) food to the Food Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partition disposal responsibilities by property type to avoid duplication and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies to follow administrator policies in consultation with policy board
rubrics_metrics.description: All of these agencies, as well as any other agencies called upon to handle special disposal problems, to follow policies laid down by the administrator in consultation with policy board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct agencies to implement centralized policy guidance from the administrator and board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator to report to Congress on needed legislation based on experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The surplus administrator to report to Congress as soon as possible on legislation needed, basing his recommendations on actual experience with the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative recommendations should be empirically grounded in disposal experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sell as much as possible early without unduly disrupting trade
rubrics_metrics.description: Sell as much as he can as early as he can without unduly disrupting normal trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor prompt disposition but avoid market disruption; balance speed and market stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heed pressure groups but act in national interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to pressure groups, but act in the national interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider stakeholder input but prioritize national economic and social goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: No sales or rentals to speculators or promoters
rubrics_metrics.description: No sales, no rentals to speculators; none to promoters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent speculative capture of surpluses that could distort markets or public benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain fair market prices; proceeds reduce national debt
rubrics_metrics.description: Get fair market prices for the values with proceeds of all sales going to reduce the national debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetize surpluses at fair value and apply proceeds to public finance objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent sales with records open to public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Sell as in a goldfish bowl, with records always open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain full transparency of disposal transactions to deter favoritism and corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use regular private trade channels when practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as practicable, use the same regular channels of trade that private business would in disposing of the particular properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage existing commercial distribution channels to maximize efficiency and market access.

rubrics_metrics.name: No government operation of surplus war plants in competition with private industry
rubrics_metrics.description: No government operation of Surplus war plants in competition with private industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid direct government competition with private firms in postwar production and disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid monopolies; ensure equal access and regional fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: No monopoly; equal access to surpluses for all businesses: preference to local ownership, but no subsidizing of one part of the country against another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent concentration of surplus assets and protect regional equity in access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrap only what must be scrapped; avoid deliberate destruction of useful property
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrap what must be scrapped, but no deliberate destruction of useful property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conserve useful assets; destruction only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure domestic productive efficiency before surplus exports
rubrics_metrics.description: Before selling surplus equipment abroad, assure America's own productive efficiency, on which our high wages and high living standards rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize domestic economic and production needs before exporting surplus goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select surplus administrator for executive capacity and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The surplus administrator to be a man of proved executive capacity, business sagacity, unquestioned integrity and great courage to fight off the selfish interests who will be seeking to exploit these surpluses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appoint a strong executive with ethical stature to resist pressure and enforce public-interest policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open facts on all sales with regular agency reports to Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: The facts on all sales to be open to public inspection, with regular reports from each disposal agency to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalize transparency and congressional oversight across disposal activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use industry advisory committees effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the disposal agencies to make effective use of industry advisory committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage private-sector expertise through advisory committees while retaining public control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow leasing, exchange and credit sales but prevent hidden government ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The disposal agencies to lease as well as sell, to exchange properties, to sell on credit—but leasing must not become a hidden device for government ownership or subsidies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flexible disposal mechanisms but guard against disguised subsidies or retained control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services to review inventories for civilian release without harming war effort
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army and Navy to examine their inventories of the most critical civilian items to see what can be safely released during the war for the civilian economy without hurting the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify items releasable to civilian economy while ensuring no adverse impact on military needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study centralization of real property handling and liquidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Surplus administrator to study how to centralize the handling of real property, also to explore the possibilities of beginning to liquidate government holdings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess centralization options for real property disposal and begin disposition planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close cooperation between WPB and surplus administrator to avoid control-induced buyer limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The closest co-operation between the War Production Board and the surplus administrator so that controls do not necessarily hinder disposition by unduly limiting potential buyers, particularly in assuring prompt disposal of small quantities of surplus materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate production controls with disposal policy to ensure effective market access, especially for small lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make full field force available to disposal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The surplus administrator and the disposal agencies to have available to them in carrying out their policies the entire field force of all of the various agencies, including the services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage interagency personnel resources to execute disposal operations efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer surpluses in lot sizes permitting participation of businesses of all sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Surpluses to be offered in lots of such size as to permit businesses of all sizes to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design lot sizes to enable small and medium enterprises to compete for surplus purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney General on policy board to prevent monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General is placed on the policy board because of the importance of preventing monopoly in disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure legal oversight to guard against anticompetitive outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau of the Budget on board to develop permanent housekeeping policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau of the Budget is on the board to develop policy for permanent good housekeeping of government properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate budgeting and long-term property-management perspectives into policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board membership should be action-capable
rubrics_metrics.description: The member [sic] of the Surplus Property Board made up of men who will carry out the decisions that are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select members committed and empowered to implement board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running review of war agencies by Bureau of the Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: A running review of the functions of all war agencies by the Bureau of the Budget, reporting regularly to the Director of War Mobilization with recommendations for cutting down the agencies as their work dwindles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously reassess agency roles and recommend de-escalation as wartime tasks decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sweat out unnecessary requirements in service programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensification of the fine work already being done in sweating out unnecessary requirements in the services' programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamline military program requirements to reduce waste and redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early review of material production/stockpiling/subsidy programs
rubrics_metrics.description: An early, equally effective review of the programs for raw material production, stockpiling, imports, subsidies and premiums to marginal producers so as not to continue any of these programs beyond being needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess continuation or termination of supply and subsidy programs as wartime needs change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review wartime material controls for modification conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Early review of all war-time material controls and limitation measures to determine under what conditions these orders can or should be modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish criteria and timing for easing material controls to resume civilian production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen industry advisory committees in WPB
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthening of the industry advisory committees in the War Production Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance private-sector advisory capacity within production policy bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tightened handling and advance planning of new contracts and cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tightened handling and advance planning of new contracts and contract cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve foresight and procedures around contracting and cancellations to reduce disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: WPB and OPA coordinate to avoid pricing delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Closer working together of the W.P.B. and the O.P.A. to avoid pricing delays in the resumption of civilian production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate production and price policy agencies to speed civilian-market reactivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Armed services to provide civilian agencies timely information
rubrics_metrics.description: The armed services to furnish all civilian agencies full information in adequate time for these agencies to do their planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require timely data-sharing from military services to enable civilian planning for reconversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian agencies should organize to use military information effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: The civilian agencies to organize themselves to use this information effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civilian bodies must have structures/processes to act on military-provided planning data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of War Mobilization to keep running conspectus of agency tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: A running conspectus by the Office of War Mobilization of the tasks assigned each agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an up-to-date inventory of agency responsibilities to coordinate demobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new demobilization agency at this time
rubrics_metrics.description: No new demobilization agency needed at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend use of existing structures rather than creating another specialized demobilization body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance 'X Day' reconversion planning for sudden enemy collapse
rubrics_metrics.description: To be prepared in event of a sudden collapse of Germany: the armed services and the War Production Board to co-operate in the immediate preparation of an 'X Day' reconversion plan based on the assumed defeat of Germany on a hypothetical date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-plan large-scale reconversion scenarios so action can be rapid if a sudden end to hostilities occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate cancellations and tentatively select industries/plants to free
rubrics_metrics.description: This plan to seek to estimate cancellation in advance: to make tentative selections of the industries and plants to be freed, to be used to get a head start on all demobilization problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify likely cancellations and targeted facilities in advance to prioritize reconversion steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance listing of civilian priorities when opening supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance listing of the priorities to be given different civilian needs in any opening up of civilian supply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefine civilian-need priorities to guide initial allocation of released production capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest priority to items improving military efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest priority to go to those things which contribute directly or indirectly to improved military efficiency, such as vital repairs, transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in reconversion, prioritize items that sustain or enhance military operations until war needs end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat competitors alike in resumption but not to harm war requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as possible, all competitors to be treated alike in the resumption of civilian production but not so as to interfere with war requirements or to hold back production of needed items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek fairness among firms when reopening civilian production, balanced against continuing military needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain war effort while planning reconversion
rubrics_metrics.description: While this advance planning is being done, no let-up on the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconversions planning must not reduce wartime operational intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt extension of key war powers where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt extension of needed war powers such as the price control law, priorities and allocations power on which functioning of War Production Board rests, requisitioning power of President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and extend statutory authorities essential for orderly wartime and transition operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney General to review expiration of agency war powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney General to study other war powers of agencies to determine when they will expire, or cutbacks as soon as they begin to think of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal review of temporary powers to set expiration/rollback conditions and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt cancellation of war contracts when goods no longer needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt cancellation of war contracts as soon as it is seen goods are no longer needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act quickly to cancel unnecessary contracts to free capacity and reduce waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement agencies to inform WPB of possible cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement agencies to inform the War Production Board of possible cancellations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure production-policy coordination by informing WPB of impending contract cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: WPB to prework policies guiding which producers to cancel or retain
rubrics_metrics.description: The W.P.B. to work out in advance the policies governing the choices as to which producers should be canceled and which left in production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop policy criteria to decide which production lines to terminate or continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make cancellation choices after full interagency consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual choices to be made after full consultation with the W.P.B., War Manpower Commission, and other interested agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-agency consultation to inform and legitimize cancellation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide contract cancellations by wartime efficiency and civilian resumption objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: That contract cancellations be guided (1) by what will contribute to a more efficient prosecution of the war and (2) by what will contribute to the quick balanced resumption of civilian production and to an orderly change-over from war to peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual criteria: minimize harm to war effort while maximizing smooth civilian reconversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate contract cancellation with procurement and civilian production expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract cancellation to be integrated with procurement and expansion of civilian production so that facilities and manpower which are released are shifted to new war work or, as far as practicable, to expanded civilian production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate cancellations to enable redeployment of assets and labor to productive uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full, frank information policy on cutbacks and cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: A full, frank information policy on all cutbacks and cancellations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate openly about reductions to manage expectations and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispose surplus in small lots to include small business
rubrics_metrics.description: Surpluses be disposed of in small lots to permit small as well as large business to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design disposal lot sizes to facilitate wide business participation, especially SMEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal agencies able to lease and sell on credit to expand small business opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Similarly, the disposal agencies to be able to lease and to sell on credit, expanding opportunities for small business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flexible sale terms to lower barriers for small-business acquisition of surpluses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective small business representation on advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective representation of small business on industry advisory committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure small-business voice in policy advisory structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect small business during resumption of civilian production
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection of small business in the resumption of civilian production, as far as is practicable without interfering with war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement measures to prevent small firms from being disadvantaged in reconversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier cancellations to favor small business conversion where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Earlier cancellations where small business can be converted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize cancellations that enable small businesses to convert to civilian production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect competitive position of small business
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Care to protect competitive position of small business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid policies that would unduly harm small-business competitiveness during reconversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relax nuisance-type production controls earlier than broader controls
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Possible relaxation of 'nuisance' type production control sooner than broader controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Easing minor regulatory controls earlier may help small producers resume operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special credit provisions to assist small business change-over
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for special credit to assist small business in the change-over and to encourage new enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial support targeted to small firms to ease reconversion costs and stimulate entrepreneurship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend Smaller War Plants Corporation lending authority for change-over finance
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Extension of the lending authority of the Smaller War Plants Corporation, at present restricted to purposes of war production, to cover financial assistance for change-over problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden an existing small-business war lending authority to include civilian transition financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand Federal Reserve authority to make industrial loans
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Expansion and liberalization of the Federal Reserve System's authority to make industrial loans permitting one-half billion dollars of such loans outstanding at any one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a significant Federal Reserve‑backed industrial-loan facility to fund reconversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplement new credit sources with private savings
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) These two additional sources of credit to supplement—not compete with—the enormous volume of savings in the hands of individuals and banks which await tapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design public credit instruments to complement, not crowd out, private-sector funding potential.
